name: Assistant access, permissions and project scope
summary: Who may use which assistant, how the user's project permissions and company boundary apply to every tool the assistant calls, how support users are recognised, and how a user gets signed in to the assistant.

roles.note: Agent access is decided by email, not by project role: the progress assistant is open to every signed-in user, and every other agent needs an internal email (an explicit allowlist or an internal domain, both set by configuration). Project data then follows the Projects API "View Project" check. Support status comes from token claims (AI-REQ-011).

actions.note: Access details for this item are handled with engineering separately.

nfr.statement: How current the assistant's view of a user's project access is. Today the check is one Projects API call per project per conversation, cached for the life of the conversation, so a role removed mid-conversation is not seen until the conversation memory expires.
nfr.open_question: How quickly must a removed project role stop assistant access (DEC-069)?

requirements.title: Every assistant request needs a verified Track3D sign-in
requirements.statement: Each assistant request must carry a Track3D access token whose signature, issuer, audience and expiry check out, and which names a user. Without one the request is refused and the chat sends the user to sign in. The progress assistant is open to every signed-in user. Every other agent, and the gateway's tool, trace, workflow and usage listings, need an internal Track3D email.

requirements.title: Project data tools check the user's View Project access first
requirements.statement: Before a project data tool runs (progress overview, alerts, schedule status, trends, project schedule, project details, sheet types, structure hierarchy and views, categories, report generation and report schedule creation or update), the assistant checks with the Projects API, using the user's own token, that the user may view every project the call targets. A refusal there stops the tool with no data. The same check runs for web chat and for direct tool calls from external AI clients, and covers any public tool that takes a project id.
requirements.rationale: Some services behind these tools (for example the progress API) were found not to enforce View Project themselves, so this check is what keeps one company's data from another user.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user with no role on project X
acceptance_criteria.when: They ask the assistant for project X's progress overview
acceptance_criteria.then: The Projects API refuses, the assistant replies that they do not have access, and no progress data is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: An external AI client signed in as that same user
acceptance_criteria.when: It calls the progress overview tool directly with project X's id
acceptance_criteria.then: The call returns an error and no data

requirements.title: Project names only resolve to the user's own company projects
requirements.statement: When the user names a project, the assistant searches only the project list the user's own token can see in their company, never all projects in the database. An unknown or ambiguous name returns candidates from that list.

requirements.title: Support status for the assistant comes from the sign-in, not a project role
requirements.statement: The web assistant treats a user as a support user when the token says role "support" or carries a support flag. External AI client sessions take the support flag from the sign-in response instead. The flag is kept server-side and stripped from what the browser receives.
